note_on_method: Two kinds of claim appear below and they are kept apart. Claims about the world, such as how many courts a park has and whether they are striped on tennis courts, come from the City of Spokane's Recreational Fields and Sports page and are cited. Claims about coverage are facts about this dataset rather than about Spokane County. The City's page had to be read in a browser, because my.spokanecity.org answers every scripted request with a redirect into a "Checking Your Browser" interstitial.

slots.coverage:
One city in Spokane County is published here: Spokane, with six venues and thirty-six courts checked against one City page. Spokane Valley, Liberty Lake, Cheney, Colbert and Millwood carry unchecked rows only, and nothing the County runs itself has been read, so none of them appears.

What this page reports is six parks whose court counts and addresses the City of Spokane publishes: four where the pickleball courts are stripes on tennis courts, two under the City's own heading "Dedicated Pickleball Courts". One park inside Spokane is named on the city page and absent here. Sky Prairie Park appears on the striped list as "Sky Prairie Park, 8501 N. Nettleton Ct., 2 Courts", and that address resolves at no house number in the Census geocoder or OpenStreetMap. Spokane County is the third county in Washington on the parent state page, after King and Clark, and the first east of the Cascades.
slots.distribution:
What we cover here sits in one city and, within it, in two parks. Mission Park holds sixteen courts and Comstock Park twelve, twenty-eight of the county's thirty-six, and each of the other four parks holds two.

The two large sets are both stripe counts. The City's tennis list gives Mission eight tennis courts and Comstock six, and its striped list gives each park exactly twice that, so what you find on the day depends on how many tennis matches are under way. Peaceful Valley's two are on one tennis court and A.M. Cannon's two are on two. Only Corbin Park and Underhill Park, two courts each, are pickleball whenever you arrive.

The six parks sit in six neighbourhoods, Logan, the South Hill, West Central, Peaceful Valley, Emerson-Garfield and East Central, across four postcodes. Indoor against outdoor cannot be drawn here at all, because the City never writes either word: thirty-six courts carry no answer on that line. No venue is stated lit and none is stated unlit. Hours are stated nowhere, and no court in the county carries a price.
slots.gaps:
This is a Spokane page under the heading of a whole county. Spokane Valley and Liberty Lake are the obvious next places and neither has been read. Neither have Cheney, Colbert, Millwood, nor anything the County runs itself.

The gaps inside the published city are gaps in what the City writes down rather than in what it has built, and they are specific. Hours: none, for any park. Lighting: none. Surface: none. Nets: not mentioned. Indoor or outdoor: neither word appears. Price: one sentence for the whole section that names a permit and no fee. Parking: nothing.

Two parks on the City's list are close to publishing and are not here. Sky Prairie Park has a count and an address the City writes as "8501 N. Nettleton Ct.", which no resolver finds. Grant Park is on the City's tennis list only, with two tennis courts, and on neither pickleball list.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in Spokane County?
faqs.a: Nobody knows the whole number. What has been checked is 36 courts across six parks, all in the City of Spokane, each with a source and a date you can see: 32 striped on tennis courts and four dedicated. The City itself lists one more park, Sky Prairie, with two courts at an address that does not resolve.

faqs.q: Are there indoor or lit courts in the county?
faqs.a: Not stated, at any venue. The City never writes "indoor" or "outdoor" against any court, and states no lighting and no hours for any park, so all six venues read as not stated on both. That is a gap in the record rather than a claim that the courts are outdoors or dark.

faqs.q: Are the courts on this page free?
faqs.a: Not stated, at any venue. The City writes one sentence for every court: they are first-come-first-served, and a court can be officially reserved with a reservation permit by online form. It publishes no price for the permit and never says the courts are free.

faqs.q: Why is Sky Prairie Park not listed?
faqs.a: The City lists it with two pickleball courts at "8501 N. Nettleton Ct.", and that address resolves at no house number in the Census geocoder or OpenStreetMap. A venue publishes here with an address that resolves as written, and no address is ever taken from outside the operator.

sources.evidence: The City's Recreational Fields and Sports page, read in a browser on 2026-09-07 because my.spokanecity.org answers scripted fetches with a 302 into a "Checking Your Browser" interstitial. Tennis & Pickleball courts are first-come-first-served, however if you would like to officially reserve a court and receive a reservation permit please fill out the online form." Under "Tennis Courts Striped for Pickleball": "A.M. Cannon Park, 1511 N. Elm St., 2 Courts", "Comstock Park, 601 W. 29th Ave., 12 Courts", "Mission Park, 1208 E. Mission Ave., 16 Courts", "Peaceful Valley Park, 1602 W. Water Ave., 2 Courts", "Sky Prairie Park, 8501 N. Nettleton Ct., 2 Courts". Under "Dedicated Pickleball Courts": "Corbin Park, 2914 N. West Oval St, 2 Courts", "Underhill Park, 2910 E. Hartson Ave., 2 Courts". Under "Tennis Courts", eleven parks including A.M. Cannon 2, Comstock 6, Corbin 1, Grant 2, Mission 8 and Peaceful Valley 1.
